content.user_title: Build Browser AI with Chrome Prompt API
content.value_statement: Browser AI teams need clear guidance for using Gemini Nano without sending user data to a server. This skill explains Chrome Prompt API setup, sessions, streaming, multimodal input, and structured output.
actual_capabilities: Explains Chrome Prompt API availability checks and model requirements.
Shows how to create sessions with parameters, monitors, and abort signals.
Covers streaming and non-streaming prompt methods for browser applications.
Documents structured output with response constraints and JSON Schema.
Describes multimodal input, session cloning, localStorage restoration, and Chrome extension use.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not install Chrome or Gemini Nano.
Prompt API support depends on Chrome version, hardware, platform, and origin trial status.
Examples require adaptation before use in production applications.
It does not replace official Chrome security or privacy review.

use_cases.title: Prototype Local Browser AI
use_cases.description: Build a proof of concept for summarization, classification, or search using the Chrome Prompt API.

use_cases.title: Plan Extension AI Features
use_cases.description: Check extension support, permissions, session handling, and user activation requirements before implementation.

use_cases.title: Design Privacy Sensitive Workflows
use_cases.description: Use local model guidance to process page content, messages, or media with reduced server exposure.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Support
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list the Chrome, hardware, storage, and platform requirements for a basic Prompt API prototype.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Session Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a Prompt API session flow with availability checks, creation options, streaming, and abort handling.

prompt_templates.title: Add Structured Output
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a structured output workflow for classification results, including schema constraints and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Extension Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review my Chrome extension AI architecture for permission policy, session lifecycle, quota management, and local storage risks.

output_examples.input: I need to know if my browser AI feature can run on user devices.
output_examples.output: A requirements checklist covering Chrome version, desktop platform support, storage, memory, model download status, and unsupported mobile platforms.

output_examples.input: I want reliable category labels from local AI output.
output_examples.output: A structured output plan that defines expected fields, validation rules, response constraints, and fallback handling for invalid or unsupported cases.

output_examples.input: I am building a Chrome extension with a local AI assistant.
output_examples.output: An implementation outline for availability checks, user activation, session creation, streaming responses, stop controls, and cleanup.

best_practices: Check availability with the same options that session creation will use.
Use streaming and abort signals for long responses or user controlled interactions.
Track input usage and destroy unused sessions to manage local resources.
anti_patterns: Assuming mobile browsers or unsupported ChromeOS devices can run the Prompt API.
Creating sessions before checking availability, permissions, and user activation requirements.
Storing sensitive conversation history without a clear retention and privacy policy.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you build local browser AI features with Chrome Prompt API and Gemini Nano.

faq.question: Does it call a remote AI service?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents local Gemini Nano usage through supported Chrome APIs.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance can support implementation planning in Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Does the Prompt API work on mobile?
faq.answer: The documented support excludes Android and iOS mobile browsers.

faq.question: What should I check before creating a session?
faq.answer: Check API availability, supported inputs and outputs, language support, permissions, and user activation requirements.

faq.question: Is this enough for production launch?
faq.answer: No. Treat it as implementation guidance and complete your own testing, privacy review, and browser compatibility checks.
